source: Minchat Shai on Gen 46:3 (the Ramah; the Masorah's census)
claim_en: al tira me-rda MITZRAYMA ('fear not to go down TO EGYPT', with the directional he): MS warns off a scribes'-correction variant without the he by the Masorah's own count — and the Ramah fixes the Torah's census of the with-he form at TWENTY-SEVEN tokens: the count verifies EXACT corpus-wide in-stream. The whole Torah's Egypt-ward traffic, counted and locked at the verse where God signs the descent.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 46:2 (the three doubled names)
claim_en: YAAQOV YAAQOV ('Jacob, Jacob'): MS's file counts THREE doubled names in Scripture with the divider stroke (paseq) between them — Abraham-Abraham at the knife (Gen 22:11), Jacob-Jacob at the border, Moses-Moses at the bush (Exod 3:4, named-and-armed) — and SNAPSHOT writes the CONNECTOR (munach) between this pair, not the divider: the mark-split carried named (the stream's own stroke checked in-stream); the doubled call answered by the singular hineni ('here I am').

source: Or Torah via Minchat Shai on Gen 46:13; Radak's scribal manual
claim_en: U-FUVA ('and Puvah'): a genuine pointing controversy — Or Torah found the vav SOFT in the Hilleli copy and the weighty books (one margin recording the dispute outright); Radak's own scribal manual rules the DAGESH — and SNAPSHOT writes the DAGESH: the stream with Radak AGAINST the Hilleli's camp, the split carried whole and the stream's side checked in-stream.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 46:21 (the Masorah)
claim_en: VA-ROSH ('and Rosh', Benjamin's son): the skeleton stands TWICE in the Torah — the son (46:21) and the Song's 'and the VENOM of serpents' (Deut 32:33, the poison-sense homograph): the head-name and the venom-word share one spelling; the Kitzur's own Scripture-pair is Lamentations' wormwood-and-poison verse (Lam 3:19, named) — he reads all ten of Benjamin's sons as memorials of the lost brother, this name for the bitterness, and the Torah's own venom-twin sharpens it.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 46:23 (the Masorah's four sevirin); the Talmud via the Kitzur
claim_en: u-VENE dan CHUSHIM ('and the SONS of Dan: Hushim'): one name under a plural header — one of the Masorah's FOUR presumed-singular (sevirin) cases: readers presume 'the son'; the letter writes the plural and the Masorah locks it (the Talmud's reed-thicket homily named by the Kitzur: one root, many stems — the one son from whom multitudes); u-vene joined by the maqqef with no stroke of its own (checked): the ledger's shortest verse, its densest grammar.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 46:26 and 46:27 (the Masorah's three-and-three)
claim_en: HA-BAA ('coming / come'): adjacent verses, the SAME word, OPPOSITE stress — END-STRESSED at the sixty-six (46:26, the caravan still in motion: one of the Masorah's three end-stressed of the form) and FORE-STRESSED at the seventy (46:27, the house counted as arrived: one of its three fore-stressed) — and MS's own mnemonic seals the adjacent pair: 'the upper one above, the lower one below' (the end-stress stroke checked in-stream; the twin asserted).

source: Minchat Shai + the readings on Gen 46:28
claim_en: LE-HOROT ('to point the way' — Judah sent ahead): the lean form stands exactly TWICE in the Torah — and its only partner is the law's own 'TO TEACH' (Lev 14:57, the leprosy-code's closing infinitive, in-corpus at lev_13's gate): the readings split Judah's errand (to clear a path / to found a house of teaching, named) — and the letter's one twin votes with the teachers: the same lean spelling points the way and teaches the law.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 46:29 (Mikhlol; the Masorah's three bindings)
claim_en: va-YESOR yosef merkavto ('and Joseph BOUND his chariot'): the alef in BARE SHEVA — the Masorah's HARD binding, landing exactly as armed at Simeon's soft one (42:24, chataf segol): a brother bound softly, a chariot bound hard for a father's face (Pharaoh's chase-binding, Exod 14:6, remains the file's last armed station); the bare-sheva alef checked in-stream.

source: Or Torah via Minchat Shai on Gen 46:6 (the Hilleli; the Ramah; the Meiri; Shemen Sason)
claim_en: MIQNEHEM ('their livestock') FULL: the printed Masorah's tangle (which confused this verse's word with another family) is untangled by Or Torah from many manuscripts, the Hilleli, the Ramah, the Meiri, and Shemen Sason — full, and SNAPSHOT writes it full: the herds of Canaan cross whole (checked).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 46:11 (the Masorah's arithmetic)
claim_en: QEHAT ('Kohath') LEAN — no vav — in every book, against a printer's emendation; MS's proof is the Masorah's own arithmetic: its note counts exactly TWO vav-prefixed Kohath tokens (both in Numbers) — were the printer's reading right, there would be three: the priest-line's grandfather crosses into Egypt lean (checked).

source: the reading tradition on Gen 46:15 (named, never merged)
claim_en: sheloshim va-SHALOSH ('thirty-three'): the subtotal counts thirty-three where the register names thirty-two — the ledger's own open question, and the readings' two answers are carried NAMED, never merged: Yocheved born between the walls, or Jacob heading his own count; the subtotal's words checked in-stream as the letter wrote them.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 46:2/3/4/21/34 (the chapter's file); the Zohar named
claim_en: The chapter's pointing file: gam AVOTENU ('also our fathers', 46:34) with the gimel DAGESHED (checked); be-MAROT ('in the visions', 46:2) LEAN with the Zohar's reading (its mirrors-partner at the Tabernacle, Exod 38:8, named), me-rda (46:3) with the resh in bare sheva, gam (46:4) soft, GERA (46:21) with the gimel dageshed, binyamin lean at his own register-head (46:21, the G65-02 census law) — all asserted.

source: Kitzur Baal HaTurim on Gen 46:2 (the crowns; named-only)
claim_en: The Kitzur's crowns-note: SEVEN crown-strokes (tagin) on the shin of le-YISRAEL ('to Israel', 46:2) — for the seven troubles survived (Esau, Laban, the angel, Dinah, Joseph, Simeon, Benjamin) after 'seven times the righteous falls and rises': scribal crowns live on the written scroll, NOT in the stream's character-set — the claim is carried NAMED-ONLY by design, and the station it decorates is checked (the token in-stream).

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:9
claim_en: THE SWEEP'S LARGEST NUMERIC ROW: A TOTAL THE TEXT'S OWN NUMBERS DO NOT REACH. The chain puts the problem in the sharpest possible form - 'have you ever seen a man given sixty-six cups and then three more, and count them as seventy?' Machine-checked in our ink, and the gap is real: 46:26 closes 'all the souls SIXTY-SIX'; 46:27 gives Joseph's sons in Egypt as TWO souls and then declares the house of Jacob SEVENTY. Sixty-six and two do not make seventy. The missing member is disputed FIVE ways on the record: Yokheved, born at the gates of Egypt; Jacob himself, by the two-legions parable in which the emperor completes whichever legion he stands with; the Holy One, who went down with them; Hushim son of Dan, counted double; and Serah daughter of Asher, who identifies herself in a later book as the one who COMPLETED the tally. The arithmetic is the corpus's own, the shortfall is in the ink, and no answer is promoted over the others.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:9
claim_en: A PLURAL HEADING OVER A SINGLE NAME, AND THE NEXT VERSE IS THE CONTROL. One of the five answers to the missing member reads 'and the SONS of Dan: Hushim' (46:23) as licensing a double count, since the heading is plural and only one name follows. Verified at the ink: the verse carries exactly three tokens - the plural construct 'and the sons of,' the name Dan, and one son - while the very next verse uses the identical plural heading over FOUR names. The contrast the argument needs is present, and the adjacent verse supplies the control. THE OTHER LEG IS DECLARED UNOPENED: the same passage records that in R. Meir's own Torah scroll the word was found written SINGULAR, 'the son of Dan' - a manuscript variant outside this corpus, which carries one consonantal text; the machine can confirm the plural it has and cannot speak to the scroll it does not.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:9
claim_en: A CAPITAL LAW AND ITS ONE EXCEPTION HANG OFF THIS BLOCK'S COUNT. Reaching the woman who says 'I am the peaceful and faithful of Israel,' the passage carries her whole case: a besieged group must NOT deliver one soul of Israel to be killed even on pain of all being killed, UNLESS he was singled out BY NAME, as Sheva son of Bikhri was. With it a distinction on whether the man is inside or outside, the rule that one who revolts against the house of David is liable to death, and the two cases that test the exception - one master who handed over a wanted man and was thereafter no longer visited by Elijah ('is that a mishnah of the pious?'), and the court that handed over a king on Sheva's precedent. A capital rule, its exception, and two applications, all arriving through a genealogy's arithmetic. The richest catch for the case-anchored shelf in Genesis.

check.note: A capital prohibition with a named-man exception and two recorded applications, reached through a discussion of a roster's count.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:6
claim_en: A LINEAGE COUNTING RULE READ OFF THE ROSTER'S OWN PHRASING. From 46:7's listing R. Yehuda bar Ilai derives that SONS' DAUGHTERS COUNT LIKE SONS, WHILE DAUGHTERS' SONS DO NOT - a descent rule extracted from how a list names its members, and the rule the next section's arithmetic actually runs on. The same passage widens the night vision's promise: 'I will also bring you up' is read as you AND ALL THE RIGHTEOUS LIKE YOU, so a personal assurance becomes a general resurrection clause; and 'Joseph will place his hand on your eyes' is read two ways, as providing for every need and as closing his eyes in death.

check.note: A rule of lineage counting derived from a roster's phrasing, with a personal promise widened into a general clause.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 96:5
claim_en: THE BURIAL DOCTRINE THAT GOVERNS THE REST OF THE BOOK, WITH A RULE ABOUT WORSHIP ATTACHED. Four reasons are recorded for refusing burial in Egypt: the land's dust was destined to become lice; lest they make him an object of worship - carrying the general rule that PUNISHMENT IS EXACTED FROM THE WORSHIPPED AS FROM THE WORSHIPPER, with two test cases; lest Egypt earn merit through him; and the land doctrine - the dead of the Land rise first, one who dies and is buried abroad dies twice, and for the righteous buried abroad the Holy One bores TUNNELS through the earth so they roll to the Land and the spirit is restored there. Read at this block and seated on the next, it is the claim the last three units' burial operators run on. 'Kindness and TRUTH' is read as the kindness done to the dead, who cannot repay.

check.note: Four recorded reasons against a foreign burial, carrying a rule that punishment reaches the worshipped, and a doctrine of subterranean transit for the righteous. SEATED CROSS-UNIT (2026-08-31 audit): this claim was anchored here but its operator lives at its home block — gen_70 claim G70-28, the burial-request operator citing Bereshit Rabbah 96:5. No gen_69 operator carries it, by design; recorded so the ID is not read as lost.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 100:5
claim_en: THE BURIAL PLOT IS AUDITED AT THE INK AND FOUND TO HAVE BEEN BOUGHT TWICE. 'In my grave that I DUG ‹כָּרִיתִי› ('kariti') for myself' is not the verb for acquiring, so the chain reads it as 'I HEAPED UP' money for it, and records the transaction: at Isaac's estate Esau took the cash and left the burial plot, at a price. Verified at the ink - the verb at 50:5 is the digging word, not the buying word, exactly as the argument requires. So the Machpelah right stands purchased twice in this corpus: the field bought from the sons of Chet at gen_39, and the share bought out from the brother here. The funeral procession is separately read as a war footing, with a doubled particle taken as an inclusion.

check.note: A burial-plot verb read as payment rather than excavation, recording a second purchase of a right the corpus already bought once. SEATED CROSS-UNIT (2026-08-31 audit): this claim was anchored here but its operator lives at its home block — gen_73, the deed-against-contest operator citing Bereshit Rabbah 100:5 (the plot twice-paid). No gen_69 operator carries it, by design; recorded so the ID is not read as lost.

source: Onkelos Genesis 46:28
claim_en: ONE CONSONANTAL WORD, AND THE TWO MEMBERS BUILD DIFFERENT INSTITUTIONS ON IT. Judah is sent ahead ‹לְהוֹרֹת› - which the chain hears as 'to TEACH,' and founds on it the first house of study, before Sinai; Onkelos reads the same letters as 'to CLEAR A PLACE before him in Goshen,' an advance party arranging quarters. The split is total and unresolvable from the ink, since both readings take the identical consonants. An academy or a billeting detail, and this corpus records both without promoting either.

check.note: One unpointed word read as teaching by the chain and as preparing quarters by the translation, yielding an academy or an advance party.

source: Onkelos Genesis 46:34; Onkelos Genesis 46:30
claim_en: THE BUFFER HOLDS TWO POLICIES TO THE END OF THE STORY. 'Every shepherd is an ABOMINATION to Egypt' becomes 'the Egyptians KEEP DISTANT from every shepherd' - the identical euphemizing move made at the separate tables three chapters earlier, held consistently. And 'NOW LET ME DIE, after seeing your face' becomes 'IF I were to die now, I WOULD BE CONSOLED' - a conditional supplied and the death-wish converted into consolation, the translation declining to let the patriarch ask for death. Two standing habits of the buffer, both visible at their last occasion in the narrative.

check.note: A taboo restated as practice and a death-wish converted to consolation, both continuing policies the translation held earlier.

source: Bereshit Rabbah 94:4; Bereshit Rabbah 94:8
claim_en: TWO LONG ARCS PASS THROUGH THIS BLOCK'S VERSES. The cedars' arc: the trees Abraham planted are cut by Jacob at Beersheba, carried to Egypt, and become the Tabernacle's boards - and this block's opening verse is the arc's middle seat. And Benjamin's ten sons at 46:21 are decoded as a ten-name memorial of the lost brother, every name a phrase of the loss. Both were recorded at earlier blocks with this roster named as where they land; both land. The roster also cashes a standing claim about Simeon's son by his sister, listed here as 'Shaul son of the Canaanite woman.'

check.note: Two multi-block arcs, a timber provenance and a memorial naming, both seated on this roster as earlier ledgers predicted.

source: Bava Batra 143b:5-7
claim_en: THE BNEI-CANON OPENS AT THIS TOKEN. One child written plural — 'the sons of Dan: Chushim' — answering whether a lone son is 'sons'; Rava's reed-thickets deflection kept on the record with the two replacement verses: a three-verse ink-canon, this token the opener. Filed F-135, auto-seated (round 34, the inheritance block).

source: Niddah 31a:24
claim_en: THE SEX-DETERMINATION RULE PROVEN FROM THE ROSTER. Unexplained until R. Tzadok read the ledger's own grammar — the sons hung on Leah, the daughter on Jacob: the attributions as proof. Filed F-171, auto-seated (round 39, the birth-and-body block).
